First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x^2.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{4-5x-2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}+3} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(\frac{-2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{5x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(-2x-\frac{5}{x}+\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})}{(1+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(\frac{-2x+0+0}{1+0}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-2x) \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
